title: Threat Detection Library - Splunk ESCU (security_content) Detection Entry
description: Schema for a single detection entry in data/splunk-escu-detections.json. Unlike every other catalogue in this library, these entries are not authored for this project — they are a curated, schema-converted subset of detections from Splunk's official, Apache-2.0-licensed 'security_content' project (https://github.com/splunk/security_content), also known as Splunk Enterprise Security Content Updates (ESCU). The catalogue spans five upstream source directories: detections/endpoint (Windows-scoped Sysmon/EDR/CrowdStrike/AppLocker telemetry, component 'Windows Endpoint', imported across two batches — an original hand-curated subset plus every remaining qualifying file; Linux-scoped Sysmon-for-Linux telemetry, component 'Linux'; macOS-scoped osquery telemetry, component 'macOS'; and Cisco Isovalent/Cilium-eBPF and Cisco Secure Client NVM container/endpoint-flow telemetry, components 'Cisco Isovalent' and 'Cisco NVM'), detections/application (ESXi syslog, Splunk's own _internal/_audit telemetry, identity-provider telemetry (Okta, PingID), Cisco appliance/MFA telemetry (ASA, Duo, IOS XE, SD-WAN), AI/LLM-abuse telemetry (AWS Bedrock, MCP servers, Microsoft 365 Copilot), and assorted other SaaS/application vendor telemetry), detections/network (Cisco network-device, Zeek/Suricata/Stream network-sensor, and other network-perimeter telemetry), detections/cloud (AWS, Azure, Microsoft 365, Google Cloud Platform, Google Workspace, Kubernetes, and GitHub audit/control-plane telemetry), and detections/web (CVE-specific web-application exploit-signature detections for individual vendor products — Ivanti, Citrix, Confluence, JetBrains TeamCity, etc. — plus Zscaler proxy telemetry) — see each entry's component field and source_url for which. Provenance fields (source_id, source_url, source_version, source_author) trace every entry back to its original file so changes upstream can be reconciled.

id.description: Namespaced sequential ID, one namespace per primary MITRE tactic.

component.description: 'Windows Endpoint', 'Linux', 'macOS', 'Cisco Isovalent', 'Cisco NVM', 'CrowdStrike', 'ESXi', 'Splunk Platform', 'Okta', 'PingID', 'Cisco ASA', 'Cisco Duo', 'Cisco IOS XE', 'Cisco SD-WAN', 'AWS Bedrock', 'MCP', 'Microsoft 365 Copilot', 'PTC Windchill', 'Application' (generic/vendor-agnostic, detections/application only), 'Cisco Network', 'Windows Network Telemetry', 'F5 BIG-IP', 'Network' (generic/vendor-agnostic), 'AWS', 'Azure', 'Microsoft 365', 'Google Cloud Platform', 'Google Workspace', 'Kubernetes', 'GitHub', 'Cloud' (generic/vendor-agnostic), 'Ivanti', 'Citrix', 'Atlassian Confluence', 'JetBrains TeamCity', 'Zscaler', 'Adobe ColdFusion', 'CrushFTP', 'Apache Tomcat', 'VMware', 'Microsoft SharePoint', 'Microsoft Exchange', 'ConnectWise ScreenConnect', 'Fortinet', or 'Web' (generic/vendor-agnostic) depending on which upstream source_url directory and platform/vendor the entry came from; kept as a field for consistency with the rest of the library's faceting.

detection_type.description: Preserved verbatim from the source project's own `type` field, unlike this library's other catalogues which use a locally-defined vocabulary.

spl.description: The source project's actual production SPL, lightly reformatted. Retains references to security_content app macros (e.g. `security_content_ctime`, per-detection `_filter` macros) that require the security_content/ESCU Splunkbase app to run as-is; see tuning_guidance.

source_id.description: The detection's stable UUID in the upstream splunk/security_content repository.

source_url.description: Permalink to the original YAML file in splunk/security_content.

source_version.description: The upstream detection's own version number at time of import.

source_author.description: The upstream detection's original author credit, preserved verbatim.

analytic_story.description: The upstream security_content 'Analytic Story' tags this detection belongs to (e.g. a ransomware family, APT campaign, or technique-family grouping) — useful for finding every detection relevant to a specific threat.
